waves.name: Whole tree behind a program registry
waves.rationale: The tree holds two programs and no JCL, scheduler or CSD, so the extractor found no entry point and the seed put no unit in any family. The validator needs at least one wave, so both programs are placed together here as one unit of work. They cannot be split on evidence: PROGA makes a computed CALL at line 9 whose target is read by ACCEPT at line 8, so PROGB could be its callee. This is a wave of last resort, not a sound family. It holds a high-high unit (PROGA) in the only wave there is, so it needs a facade first: a registry that maps the run-time program name to a known target and rejects any name not on the list. Confidence is low because the real entry points, callee set and schedule are outside the tree.
waves.unblocks: Nothing that can be shown from this tree. It would unblock the wave plan for the rest of the system once the JCL and scheduler are supplied, because the registry list is the first thing those files must fill in.
